epic.title: Home network: four networks on the RT-AX86U, one DNS filter, VPN only
epic.description:
Four networks on the RT-AX86U on Asuswrt-Merlin (Trusted, Work, Smart devices, Guests) with names that reveal nothing; one network-wide DNS filter carrying the security lists and the topic 9 blocking; remote access through a VPN only, port 3389 never exposed; the ASUS the only router if 4th Utility allows it; smart devices given the least internet they need; cameras and the baby monitor local only. Settings as scripts in a git repo, each change approved by Phil; as strong as possible inside the £100, invisible-to-Kirsty and simple-mode answers.

## Order
Audit both routers first (net.01), then the single-router question (net.02) and the three research notes (net.03 filter, net.04 remote access) in parallel. The design (net.05) follows the audit and net.02, then the settings repo (net.06), then the build one network per sitting (net.07). Devices move after: the work laptop (net.08), smart devices room by room (net.09), the guest card (net.10), with Kirsty's fallback (net.20) ready before the room moves. Then internet rules per device (net.12), TV tracking (net.13) and cameras local (net.14, after the VPN in sub.07). The inventory (net.15) feeds alerts (net.16), the 2am test (net.17, after sub.09) and the cull list (net.19). Remote access guide (net.21) after net.04, then the work laptop route (net.22). Attack test (net.23), the monthly review from 2026-12-28 (net.24), and the done check (net.26). Grandad's PC (net.25) any time.

## Done means
The four networks hold, the work laptop sees nothing else, the VPN is the only way in, and the monthly review keeps it so.

## Flags
- H2.14 [claude]: work laptop remote access on the Everlight-sanctioned route only (net.22); not reopened.

## Dossier
The dossier is attached in Docs.

tickets.title: Audit both routers (4th Utility and the RT-AX86U) and an outside scan: open ports, WPS, remote admin, UPnP, firmware
tickets.description:
## What
Phil opens each router's admin page and writes down five settings (WPS, remote admin from the internet, UPnP, port forwards and DMZ, firmware version); Claude Code then scans Phil's own public address from outside the house (a phone hotspot) and from the PC, and writes a one-page report into this ticket. Nothing is changed in this sitting except what Phil chooses to switch off on the spot (WPS and remote admin are safe to turn off).

## Why
Section 2 answer 14: "not sure" what is open, so the first ticket is an audit of both routers plus an outside scan. Behind double NAT the outside world sees the 4th Utility router first.

## Done looks like
The five settings recorded for both routers in the answer boxes; a scan report on the ticket listing every open port seen from outside and what it is; any change made written down with the time.

## Unlocks
net.02 (whether the ASUS can be the only router), net.05 (the design starts from what is really there), net.23 (the later attack test compares against this).

## Depends on
Nothing.

steps_definition.title: Audit both routers and scan from outside

intro.answer: Two routers, five settings each, one outside scan: you will know exactly what the internet can reach.
to_hand: The admin passwords for both routers (in Proton Pass)
Your phone with mobile data for the hotspot

sources.label: 4th Utility: can I supply my own router?

phases.title: Read the two routers
needs: A pen or this page open

steps.title: Open the ASUS admin page
steps.body_html: Open router.asus.com and sign in. On the first page note the firmware version shown at the top.
steps.expect_html: The Network Map page, with a firmware line such as 3004.388.13.

steps.title: ASUS: WPS, remote admin, UPnP, port forwards
steps.body_html:
Check four pages and write what you see:

  • Wireless, WPS: on or off. Turn it off.
  • Administration, System: "Enable Web Access from WAN" should be No; SSH "LAN only" or off.
  • WAN, Internet Connection: "Enable UPnP" on or off (leave it as is for now, just note it).
  • WAN, Virtual Server / Port Forwarding and WAN, DMZ: list any rules.
steps.expect_html: WPS off, web access from WAN off, and a written list of any forwards.

notes.html: Switching WPS and remote admin off breaks nothing in the house.

steps.title: 4th Utility router: the same four settings
steps.body_html: The address and admin password are on the label under the router. Look for WPS, remote management, UPnP, port forwarding and DMZ, and the firmware version. Write each down; turn WPS off if it is on.
steps.expect_html: Five answers recorded for the 4th Utility router.

fields.label: 4th Utility port forwards or DMZ
fields.placeholder: none, or the ports and which address

troubleshooting.symptom: The admin page asks for a password that is not on the label
troubleshooting.fix: Leave it; ask Claude to note it on this ticket. 4th Utility support can reset it; do not factory-reset the router, it would take the house offline.

steps.title: Read your public address
steps.body_html: On the Network Map, click the Internet icon and note the WAN IP. Behind double NAT this will be a private address (192.168.x.x); the public one is on the 4th Utility router's status page.
steps.expect_html: A public address written in the box (it is not a secret, but it stays in this ticket only).

fields.label: Public IP address of the house

steps.title: Claude Code scans from outside

where.label: Claude Code on the PC, joined to the phone hotspot

steps.body_html: Join the PC to the phone's hotspot, then paste the prompt below into Claude Code. It scans only the address you recorded, and only common ports, then writes the report into this ticket.
steps.expect_html: A report on the ticket: each open port, what answered, and a plain-English verdict.

blocks.label: Prompt
blocks.text: Scan only the public address recorded in the answers of this ticket (it is Phil's own house). From this PC on the phone hotspot, run a TCP scan of the 1,000 most common ports and a UDP check of 53, 123, 500, 1900 and 4500 with standard tools. Then rejoin the home network and scan both routers' LAN addresses for open admin ports. Write a one-page report into this ticket: port, service, which router, risk, suggested fix. Change nothing.

notes.html: Scan only addresses that are yours. Never point the tools at anything else.

steps.title: Read the report and tick
steps.body_html: Read the report. If anything is open that you did not know about, add one line saying keep or close; Claude Code closes nothing without that line.
steps.expect_html: Every open port has keep or close next to it.

tickets.title: Research: can the ASUS be the only router (4th Utility modem mode or bridge), and what it means for the broadband decision
tickets.description:
## What
Claude writes a short research note on the ticket: 4th Utility says customers may use their own router, supplying a free Bridge where the fibre ends and a PPPoE login under Service Info in the online account, and warns that you "cannot pre-configure your set-up and then go back". The note lists what to ask 4th Utility in writing first (the Bridge, the PPPoE username, any VLAN id, IPv6), the exact RT-AX86U WAN settings, a rollback plan, and whether to do the swap before or after the broadband review on 2027-03-01. Nothing is switched over in this run.

## Why
Section 2 answer 18: make the ASUS the only router if 4th Utility allows it. It ends double NAT, which also decides whether the router's own VPN can work (net.04).

## Done looks like
A note on the ticket with the questions for 4th Utility, the settings, the rollback, a recommendation on timing against fin.15, and the sources with dates.

## Unlocks
net.05 (the design knows how many routers there are), net.04 (the router-VPN branch), fin.15 (the broadband review gets the answer).

## Depends on
net.01: the audit shows what the 4th Utility router is doing today.

tickets.title: Research: where the DNS filter runs (router, Substrate box, hosted); the 26 November guide is input
tickets.description:
## What
Claude compares three homes for the one network-wide DNS filter: AdGuard Home on the RT-AX86U through the Merlin installer, a filter on the Substrate box (sub.06), and a hosted service (NextDNS or Control D). For each: cost, per-person profiles (Phil, Kirsty unfiltered for news, guests, a future child), how it is forced on every device (Merlin DNS Director), whether it follows the phones away from home, the "open anyway" mechanism and the HTTPS block-page limit (see dossiers/block.md section 3.1), and what happens when it is down. The 26 November NextDNS guide is read as input only. The note ends with a recommendation for Phil to approve.

## Why
Section 2 answers 11 and 12: one filter carrying both security lists and the topic 9 blocking, and where it runs decided in a research ticket. H10: the 26 November guide is input, not plan.

## Done looks like
A comparison table and a one-line recommendation on the ticket, with sources dated; Phil's approve or change recorded as a comment.

## Unlocks
sub.06 (the filter service is built where this decides), block.03 (profiles), block.04 (lists), block.05 (the block page design).

## Depends on
Nothing.

## Red team
- Finding 30: A hosted filter is chosen only on a free tier or with Phil's yes to the cost.

tickets.title: Research: remote access, the July Tailscale and Remote Desktop set-up against the router's own VPN; 3389 never exposed
tickets.description:
## What
Claude compares the July plan (Tailscale on the PC and laptop, Remote Desktop to the PC's tailnet name, Windows Pro host, NLA on) with the RT-AX86U's built-in WireGuard and OpenVPN servers, and with Tailscale on the router or on the Substrate box as a subnet router. For each: does it work through today's double NAT (the router VPN does not until net.02 ends it), what Kirsty's phone needs, how the cameras are reached for net.14, the Tailscale Personal plan's six users and 50 tagged resources, and how it fails. Ends with one recommended route for Phil to approve. Port 3389 is never forwarded in any option.

## Why
H2 item 13: a research ticket decides between the July set-up and the router's own VPN, then one Field guide covers every device. Section 2 answer 13: remote access through a VPN only.

## Done looks like
A comparison on the ticket with a recommended route; Phil's approval recorded.

## Unlocks
sub.07 (the VPN service), net.21 (the remote access guide), net.14 (cameras over the VPN).

## Depends on
Nothing for Tailscale; net.02 for the router-VPN branch (double NAT).

tickets.title: Network design: four networks (Trusted, Work, Smart devices, Guests), names that reveal nothing, within what the RT-AX86U firmware allows; diagram to Docs
tickets.description:
## What
Claude designs the four networks for the RT-AX86U on Asuswrt-Merlin 3004.388, which has no VLAN or Guest Network Pro page (those need a 3006 model such as the RT-AX86U Pro). The likely layout: main network = Trusted; Guest Network 1 (its own subnet) = Smart devices on 2.4 GHz; Guest Network 2 = Work; Guest Network 3 = Guests; each with Access Intranet off. The design says which wired devices (TVs, Sky Glass, the Substrate box) cannot be separated without a VLAN script or another routing device, and prices those options for Phil without choosing. Network names reveal nothing about Phil or the house. A diagram and the address plan go to Docs.

## Why
Section 2 answers 8, 16 and 29, and 2b names: four networks, the managed switches used where they help separation, names that reveal nothing.

## Done looks like
A design page in Docs with the diagram, the four names, subnets, which device kinds go where, what the switches do, and the open choice for wired separation with prices or "to be priced".

## Unlocks
net.06 (the settings repo starts from this design), net.07 (the build), net.11 (the kit list).

## Depends on
net.01 (what is there now) and net.02 (one router or two).

## Cost
Any replacement router or VLAN-capable kit is listed with a price or "to be priced"; nothing is bought in this run.

## Red team
- Finding 8: Check first: confirm which of the four-network design Asuswrt-Merlin on the RT-AX86U can do natively and which needs a script or a managed switch, before anything is built.

tickets.title: Settings-as-scripts repo for the router: dated config backups, every change a reviewed commit, applied by Claude Code
tickets.description:
## What
Claude creates a private git repo for the router's settings: a dated backup of the RT-AX86U configuration (Administration, Restore/Save/Upload Setting, plus the JFFS partition) before every change, the network design as readable settings files, and a script per change that Claude Code applies over SSH only after Phil approves the commit. Each change carries its rollback. No secret (Wi-Fi passwords, admin password) is committed in plain text; they stay in Proton Pass and are entered by Phil.

## Why
2b method: settings as scripts in a git repo, applied by Claude Code, each change approved by him. Section 2 answer 28: dated config backups.

## Done looks like
The repo exists with a first dated backup, the design as files, a README with the apply and rollback steps, and one dry-run change reviewed by Phil.

## Unlocks
net.07 (the build is applied from this repo).

## Depends on
net.05 (the design to encode).

## Red team
- Finding 8: A full config backup is taken and a restore of it rehearsed before the first applied change; every applied change has a one-step revert.

tickets.title: Build the four networks on the ASUS (Merlin): SSIDs, isolation rules, within what the firmware allows
tickets.description:
## What
Phil builds the four networks from the net.05 design on the RT-AX86U, one network per sitting: Smart devices on Guest Network 1 (2.4 GHz, its own subnet), Work on Guest Network 2, Guests on Guest Network 3, each with Access Intranet off, then the main network (Trusted) tidied last and the 4th Utility router's Wi-Fi turned off. Claude Code takes a dated backup from the settings repo before each sitting. No device is moved here; moves are net.08 to net.10.

## Why
Section 2 answer 8: four networks, Trusted, Work, Smart devices, Guests. 2b bar: as strong as possible inside the earlier answers.

## Done looks like
All four networks broadcast with the design's names; from each non-Trusted network the router admin page and the PC cannot be reached; a backup exists for each step.

## Unlocks
net.08, net.09, net.10 (moving devices), net.18 (tripwires), net.20 (Kirsty's fallback), net.21 (remote access), net.23 (attack testing), net.24 (the monthly review).

## Depends on
net.06 (the settings repo and backups).

## Red team
- Finding 8: Applied only while Phil is in the house with the admin page open on a wired or second device; the Trusted network is built last so the PC never loses its path.

tickets.title: Move the Everlight work laptop to Work; isolate and see
tickets.description:
## What
Phil joins the Everlight work laptop to the Work network, forgets the old network on it, and checks that work still works (Everlight's own VPN, Teams or equivalent) while the laptop can no longer see the PC, printers or smart devices. If work breaks, he moves it back and writes what broke.

## Why
Section 2 answer 7 and 2b: the work machine is on the same Wi-Fi as everything else today; employer policy not checked first, "isolate it and see".

## Done looks like
The laptop on Work; work apps working; the PC not visible from it; result recorded.

## Unlocks
net.22 (work laptop remote access), net.26 (done check).

## Depends on
net.07 (the Work network exists).

## Red team
- Finding 42: Revert path in the same sitting; if the laptop's own VPN or management agents stop working it goes back to Trusted and the question goes to IT.

steps_definition.title: Move the work laptop to the Work network

intro.answer: One laptop, one network, one check that work still works.

steps.title: Join Work and forget the old network
steps.body_html: Join the Work network (name from the design page). Then forget the old network so the laptop does not drift back.
steps.expect_html: The laptop shows it is connected to Work only.

notes.html: If Everlight's settings stop you forgetting a network, just join Work and note it.

steps.title: Check work still works
steps.body_html: Connect Everlight's VPN, open email and Teams (or whatever you use) and one work system.
steps.expect_html: Everything work-related works as before.

troubleshooting.fix: Move the laptop back to the old network, note the error here; Claude will look at it.

steps.title: Check it is isolated
steps.body_html: Type \\ followed by the PC's name in the File Explorer bar, and open router.asus.com.
steps.expect_html: Neither opens.

tickets.title: Move the smart devices (cameras, doorbell, plugs, bulbs, sensors, Alexa, TVs, sticks) to Smart devices, one sitting per room
tickets.description:
## What
Phil moves every smart device to the Smart devices network, one room per sitting, checking each from its app before the next. Devices that will not move or stop working go back on the old network and onto the net.12 list. Shared TVs and Alexa are Kirsty's too: tell her the evening before each room.

## Why
Section 2 answers 3 and 5: a smart device taken over and reaching the PC is one of the four worries.

## Done looks like
Every smart device listed per room and working on the Smart devices network, or written down as an exception.

## Unlocks
net.12 (internet rules per device), net.15 (inventory), wall.24 (wall screens on Smart devices).

## Depends on
net.07 (the network exists).

tickets.title: Smart devices and the internet: block where the device still works, else allow only its own cloud; per device
tickets.description:
## What
For every device on the Smart devices network, Claude Code proposes a rule from a week of DNS logs (block the internet entirely if the device still works locally, otherwise allow only its own cloud's domains), as a reviewed commit in the router repo; Phil approves per group and checks each device still works the next day.

## Why

Nothing in E.net; closes an account-hygiene loose end.
